requirements.source_title: Organizational Accountability for Cybersecurity
requirements.source_text: /2/1439H, makes NCA the cybersecurity regulator in the Kingdom and the national reference for anything related to cybersecurity. NCA’s mandate and duties fulfill the strategic and regulatory cybersecurity needs related to the development of cybersecurity national policies, governance mechanisms, frameworks, standards, controls and guidelines. The NCA’s mandate and duties also fulfill the need to continuously monitor the compliance of organizations to support the important role of cybersecurity, which has increased with the rise of security risks in cyberspace more than any time before. NCA’s mandate states that its responsibility for cybersecurity does not absolve any government, private or other organization from its own cybersecurity responsibilities as confirmed by Royal Decree
requirements.source_summary: The requirement identifies the NCA as the Kingdom’s cybersecurity regulator and national reference for cybersecurity matters, including national policies, governance mechanisms, frameworks, standards, controls, guidelines, and compliance monitoring. It also emphasizes that the NCA’s role does not remove an organization’s own responsibility for managing and maintaining its cybersecurity obligations.

requirements.source_text: through decision support and is an economic resource to support competitiveness at the national level, where national organizations collect and process vast amounts of data that may be vulnerable to cyber threats and risks that negatively impact national security, the Kingdom's economy, reputation, external relations, or critical infrastructures, which raises the urgency to put cybersecurity requirements to protect against such threats and risks.The NCA’s mandate as per the Royal Decree
requirements.source_summary: The requirement highlights that national organizations collect and process significant volumes of economically and strategically important data that may be exposed to cyber threats. Such threats could adversely affect national security, the economy, reputation, external relations, or critical infrastructure, creating an urgent need for cybersecurity requirements that protect against these risks. It also references the NCA’s mandate under the Royal Decree.

requirements.source_title: Continuous Compliance and NCA Assessment Readiness
requirements.source_text: /11/1439H, all organizations within the scope of these controls must implement whatever necessary to ensure continuous compliance with the controls, which cannot be achieved without achieving continuous compliance with the Essential Cybersecurity Controls (ECC –1: 2018) where applicable. NCA evaluates organizations’ compliance with the DCC through multiple means such as self-assessments by the organizations, and/or external assessments, in accordance with the mechanisms deemed appropriate by NCA.
requirements.source_summary: Organizations within the scope of the controls should implement the measures necessary to maintain continuous compliance. Where applicable, this includes maintaining continuous compliance with the Essential Cybersecurity Controls (ECC –1: 2018). Organizations should also be prepared for NCA compliance evaluations, which may use self-assessments, external assessments, or other mechanisms determined appropriate by NCA.

requirements.source_title: Identity and Access Management for Sensitive Data
requirements.source_text: , cybersecurity requirements for identity and access management must cover at least the following:PublicConfidentialSecretTop Secret2-1-1-1Strict restriction toallow only the minimum number of personnel accessing, viewingand sharingdata based on lists of privileges limited to Saudi-national employees unless exempted bythe Authorizing Official(the head of the organization or his/her delegate) and those lists are approved by the Authorizing Official.2-1-1-2Prohibiting the sharing of approved lists of privileges with unauthorized persons.2-1-2Managing identities and access rights to view data using Privileged Access Management systems.2-1-3In addition to ECC subcontrol
requirements.source_summary: The requirement states that cybersecurity requirements for identity and access management must restrict access, viewing, and sharing of Public, Confidential, Secret, and Top Secret data to the minimum necessary personnel. Access privileges must be defined in approved lists, limited to Saudi-national employees unless the Authorizing Official grants an exemption, and protected from unauthorized disclosure. Identities and access rights for viewing data must be managed using Privileged Access Management systems. The source also refers to an additional ECC subcontrol, but does not provide its details.

requirements.source_title: Third-Party Data Security and Sharing Requirements
requirements.source_text: , cybersecurity requirements for third-parties cybersecurity must include at least the following:PublicconfidentialSecretTop Secret3-1-1-1Screening orvetting third-party employees who have access to the data.3-1-1-2Requiring contractual commitment by third-partiesto securely dispose the organization’s data at the end of the contract or in case of contract termination, including providing evidences of such disposal to the organization.3-1-1-3Documentingall data sharing operations within third-parties, including data sharing justification. 3-1-1-4When transferring data outside the kingdom, the capability of the hosting organization abroad to safeguard data must be verified, approval ofthe Authorizing Officialmust be obtained and complyingwith related laws and regulations. 3-1-1-5Requiring third-parties to notify the organization immediately in case of cybersecurity incident that may affect data that has been shared or created.3-1-1-6Reclassifying data to the least level to achieve the objective before sharing it with third-parties using data masking or data scrambling techniques.3-1-2In alignment with relatedlaws and regulations, and in addition to the applicable controls in ECC and controls within DCC domain
requirements.source_summary: The requirement establishes minimum cybersecurity conditions for third parties that access, receive, host, share, or create organizational data. These conditions include screening or vetting relevant third-party personnel; contractual obligations for secure data disposal and disposal evidence; documentation and justification of data-sharing activities; verification and approval for transfers outside the Kingdom in accordance with applicable laws and regulations; immediate notification of incidents affecting shared or created data; and reducing data classification to the lowest appropriate level through masking or scrambling before sharing. Implementation must also align with applicable laws, regulations, and other referenced controls.

todo.description: Implement a third-party data security process that identifies data shared with each third party, records the business justification and classification, applies masking or scrambling where appropriate, verifies personnel screening, embeds secure disposal and incident-notification obligations in contracts, and obtains required verification and approval before transferring data outside the Kingdom.
